title: Lisse section rigidity on integral henselian test pairs
statement:
Let $A,B,C$ be commutative rings with unital homomorphisms $A\to B$ and $A\to C$, and let $I\subseteq A$ be an ideal. Assume $B$ is integral over $A$, meaning every element satisfies a monic polynomial over $A$, that $C$ is w-contractible [sk-def-pe-wlocal], and that $(C,IC)$ is a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Put
$$D=B\otimes_A C,\qquad T=\operatorname{Spec}D,\qquad T_0=\operatorname{Spec}(D/ID),$$
where $ID=(IC)D$, and let $a:T_0\hookrightarrow T$ be the quotient closed immersion and $b:T\to\operatorname{Spec}B$ the projection [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then $D$ is integral over $C$, $(D,ID)$ is a henselian pair, both $D$ and $D/ID$ are w-strictly local [sk-def-pe-wlocal], and the actual map
$$\pi_0(a):\pi_0(T_0)\longrightarrow\pi_0(T)$$
is a homeomorphism of component spaces with their quotient topology [lem-pe-spectral-components-profinite].

Let $\Lambda$ be any commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], with $\Lambda_Y=p_Y^*\Lambda$ on each small pro-etale site [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use internal module sheaves and ordinary unbounded derived categories, with K-injective total right derived direct images, in compatible universes [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, def-weil-size-convention]. For every finite-rank lisse $\Lambda_{\operatorname{Spec}B}$-module $L$ (pro-etale locally finite free, rank zero and varying ranks allowed [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]), $M=b^*L$ is finite-rank lisse and the canonical restriction is an isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$:
$$R\Gamma(T,M[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma(T_0,a^*M[0]).$$
Here the map is induced by the actual derived adjunction unit for $a$, followed by the canonical derived composition comparison, and $R\Gamma$ means total right derived global sections followed by forgetting scalars. No finiteness or finite presentation of $B/A$ or $D/C$, Noetherianity, or completeness or discreteness of $\Lambda$ is required. Zero algebras and empty spectra are included; no w-contractibility assertion for $D$ is made.

proof.text: Apply integral base change to $A\to B$ and $A\to C$. It makes $C\otimes_A B$ integral over $C$; the flip $c\otimes b\mapsto b\otimes c$ identifies this $C$-algebra with $D$. Apply integral permanence of henselian pairs to $(C,IC)$ and $C\to D$. Thus $(D,(IC)D)=(D,ID)$ is henselian. Neither input requires an injective or finite ring map.

Put $S=\operatorname{Spec}C$, which is qcqs by the affine qcqs lemma. Form the quasi-coherent algebra $\widetilde D$: the tilde-sections construction gives sections $D_f$ on $D(f)\subset S$, and multiplication is the ordinary multiplication of fractions, compatible with restriction. Its global sections are $D$. For an affine open $U\subset S$, the affine algebra restriction lemma identifies its sections with $D\otimes_C\mathcal O_S(U)$; integral base change therefore verifies integrality on every such $U$. Apply the integral-algebra approximation lemma, clause (2), to $\widetilde D$. It gives a nonempty directed system of finite and finitely presented quasi-coherent algebras $\mathcal D_i$ with colimit $\widetilde D$. The affine-sections colimit lemma gives $D\cong\varinjlim_i D_i$, where $D_i=\mathcal D_i(S)$ are finite as $C$-modules and finitely presented as $C$-algebras by the approximation lemma's stated affine definitions. All maps are $C$-algebra maps. Choose the indexing data in the compatible universes of the statement. No inclusion of $D_i$ into $D$ is required.

source.place: Tag 0817 (lemma-integral-algebra-directed-colimit-finite (2)); Tag 01ID (lemma-colimit-quasi-coherent), affine sections; affine localization construction of the associated algebra.

proof.text: Apply the ind-finite contractible-base lemma to the $C$-algebra system $(D_i)$ of step 2. Its base is w-contractible by hypothesis, and each stage has both required finiteness properties. Thus $D$ is w-strictly local, even when the transition maps are noninjective. Apply henselian w-strict locality invariance to the pair $(D,ID)$ from step 1: it gives w-strict locality of $D/ID$. This uses only weak strict locality of $D$, without imposing extremal disconnectedness on its components.

source.place: Lemma 2.1.9 and Example 2.2.2 through the existing ind-finite lemma; Lemma 2.2.13 for the henselian quotient.

proof.text: Apply the first clause of condensed henselian lisse rigidity to $A=D$, $I=ID$ and the given condensed ring $\Lambda$. Henselianity is step 1. It identifies the actual induced map $\pi_0(a):\pi_0(T_0)\to\pi_0(T)$ as a homeomorphism with the component quotient topologies. This clause is unconditional: the later w-contractibility condition in that lemma is needed only for its derived-category equivalence, which is not used here.

source.place: Corollary 4.4(1), independent of the additional condition in Corollary 4.4(2).

proof.text: Pull back a pro-etale cover trivializing $L$ along $b$. Inverse image preserves this cover and its finite free trivializations, using the canonical coefficient and module-pullback composition comparisons. Thus $M=b^*L$ is finite-rank lisse, with the same possibly varying ranks and with rank zero allowed. Apply w-strict lisse component cohomology to $h=a$, $X=T$, $X'=T_0$ and $M$. Steps 3 and 4 supply exactly its weak strict locality and component-homeomorphism hypotheses. Its conclusion is the asserted isomorphism in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, for arbitrary condensed $\Lambda$. Its map is explicitly induced by the actual adjunction unit and canonical pullback comparisons, so it is the stated restriction after the derived composition comparison, rather than an unspecified isomorphism of section objects. That lemma permits empty spectra; all preceding algebraic inputs permit the zero algebra. None uses Noetherianity, completeness or discreteness.
